import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' not found. Please ensure the dataset is in the correct directory.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Clean up data: drop rows with missing breed or year, ensure year is integer
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Rasse1Text', 'StichtagDatJahr']).copy()
df_clean['StichtagDatJahr'] = df_clean['StichtagDatJahr'].astype(int)

# Identify the most recent year in the dataset
latest_year = df_clean['StichtagDatJahr'].max()

# Find the top 10 most popular breeds in the most recent year
# We identify the top 9 purebreds first to avoid "Mischling" (Mixed Breed) dominating the list
top_purebreds = df_clean[
    (df_clean['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year) &
    (~df_clean['Rasse1Text'].str.contains('Mischling', case=False, na=False))
]['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(9).index.tolist()

# Add "Mischling" to our list, as it's a very common and important category
top_breeds_list = top_purebreds + ['Mischling']

# Filter the entire dataset to only include these top breeds across all years
df_top_breeds = df_clean[df_clean['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds_list)]

# Group by year and breed to get the annual count for plotting
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# --- Visualization ---
# Set a modern plot style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')

# Create the plot figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Generate the line plot showing trends for each breed
sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    palette='tab10',
    linewidth=2.5,
    marker='o',
    markersize=5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Formatting and Labels ---
# Set title and axis labels with descriptive text
min_year, max_year = breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].min(), breed_trends['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
ax.set_title(
    f'Popularity of Top Dog Breeds in Zurich ({min_year}–{max_year})',
    fontsize=20,
    pad=25,
    fontweight='bold'
)
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Customize ticks to be clear and readable
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=12)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=12)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MaxNLocator(integer=True)) # Ensure x-axis ticks are whole numbers for years

# Customize the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually rename "Mischling" for better understanding
try:
    mischling_index = labels.index('Mischling')
    labels[mischling_index] = 'Mixed Breed (Mischling)'
except ValueError:
    pass # 'Mischling' was not in the top breeds

# Place legend outside the plot area for better visibility
ax.legend(
    handles,
    labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 1),
    loc='upper left'
)

# Improve aesthetics by removing top and right spines
sns.despine()

# Add a subtle horizontal grid
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='-', alpha=0.2)

# Save the figure
# bbox_inches='tight' ensures that the legend is not cut off
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
